According to the latest issue of the *Power On* newsletter, Apple was reportedly considering adding a feature to its "Apple Upgrade" program that would make setting up a new iPhone almost seamless: pre-transferring the user's data to the new device. In the end, however, the feature never came to fruition.

The concept is simple: if a user upgrades regularly through fixed monthly instalments, why not make switching to a new phone as convenient as possible? Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reports:

There are some obvious gaps here. First, your iCloud backup would be slightly out of date, because data can only be transferred at the moment of shipment — that is, a few days after the order is placed — unless you choose to pick up the device in person at the store.

In addition, there is an obvious privacy concern. Having said that, if you have been using iCloud backup all along, it should come as no surprise that Apple has your data. But the average user might worry about how the data gets to the new phone and whether anyone has handled it along the way.

Two years ago, Apple rolled out a brand-new system across its retail stores called "Presto," which lets staff update the software while the iPhone is still in its box. It's easy to imagine this system being expanded in the future to support iCloud backup transfers, with no one touching your data throughout the process.

However, the feature ultimately never made it to market — and that may actually be a good thing.
